fact: KINIX (Kinshasa Internet Exchange), founded in 2012 and run by ISPA-DRC as one of three community IXPs of the RDC-IX project, was operating with more than 20 participating networks when it relocated its infrastructure into the Raxio DRC data centre in Kinshasa, per Raxio Group's 20 August 2026 statement.

ACIX (Africa Congo Internet Exchange), established in 2023 and operated by DE-CIX for the NGO Internet pour Tous, was in service in Kinshasa and expanded to a second data-centre site in OADC Texaf's Kinshasa FIH1 facility, per ITWeb Africa on 19 May 2026.
Tech Africa says KINIX, founded in 2012, carries 23 participating networks across 25 connections, including all four major mobile operators.
Tech Africa says Meta and Cloudflare both peer at KINIX.
KINIX says it currently exchanges more than 1 terabit per second and expects to pass 2 Tbps after the Raxio deployment.

Tech Africa says networks registered outside the DRC peer at KINIX, including GVA in Cote d'Ivoire, Paratus and AFR-IX Telecom, and that exchange points in Goma and Lubumbashi serve the east and south.
Internet Society says the Kinshasa Internet Exchange (KINIX), built by ISPA-DRC in November 2012, has increased local internet traffic from a few Mbps to close to 80 Gbps over ten years.
Internet Society says ISPA-DRC launched a second IXP in Lubumbashi (LUBIX) in 2019 and a third in Goma (GOMIX), operating since 2021.
ISOC Pulse's IXP Tracker lists 4 exchange points in the DR Congo with 26 of 51 networks peering.
ISPA-DRC says its KINIX exchange, launched November 2012, had 23 peers and an 84 Gbps traffic peak in August 2024.
ISPA-DRC's deck shows Google and Facebook caches connected at KINIX and sets out a model for filling caches connected to its exchanges.
